entries.title: Psalms 32:1
segments:
PSALM XXXII. 
 
  The happiness of them whose sins are forgiven, ver. 1, 2.   The necessity of confessing our sins, and of prayer, ver. 3-6.   God's promise to them that trust in him, ver. 7-10.   An exhortation to rejoice in God, ver. 11.   A psalm of David, Maschil. 
 
Title of the psalm.  Maschil-Or, an instructor.  This psalm is fitly so called, because it was composed for the information of the church, in that most important doctrine, the way to true blessedness.

entries.title: Psalms 32:2
segments: V. 2. Imputeth-Whom God doth not charge with the guilt of his sins, but graciously pardons and accepts him in Christ.  No guile-Who freely confesses all his sins, and turns from sin to God with all his heart.

entries.title: Psalms 32:3
segments: V. 3. Silence-From a full and open confession of my sins.  Old-My spirit failed, and the strength of my body decayed.  Roaring-Because of the continual horrors of my conscience, and sense of God's wrath.

entries.title: Psalms 32:4
segments: V. 4. Hand-Thy afflicting hand.  My moisture-Was dried up.

entries.title: Psalms 32:5
segments: V. 5. The iniquity-The guilt of my sin.

entries.title: Psalms 32:6
segments: V. 6. For this-Upon the encouragement of my example.  Found-In an acceptable and seasonable time, while God continues to offer grace and mercy.  Waters-In the time of great calamities.  Not come-So as to overwhelm him.

entries.title: Psalms 32:8
segments: V. 8. I will-This and the next verse seems to be the words of God, whom David brings in as returning this answer to his prayers. Mine eye-So Christ did St. Peter, when he turned and looked upon him.

entries.title: Psalms 32:9
segments: V. 9. Will not-Unless they be forced to it by a bit or bridle. And so all the ancient translators understand it.

entries.title: Psalms 32:10
segments: V. 10. Sorrows-This is an argument to enforce the foregoing admonition.
